steps.whatIf:
class MockIdentityMap:
    def __init__(self):
        self.map = {}  # (Model, ID) -> Object Instance

    def load(self, model_cls, pk, name):
        key = (model_cls, pk)
        if key in self.map:
            return self.map[key], True  # Cache hit (Same instance)
        instance = {"pk": pk, "name": name, "dirty": False}
        self.map[key] = instance
        return instance, False

identity_map = MockIdentityMap()
user1, cached1 = identity_map.load("User", 42, "Alice")
user2, cached2 = identity_map.load("User", 42, "Alice")

# Modify attribute
user1["name"] = "Alice Cooper"
user1["dirty"] = True

print("=== IDENTITY MAP PHYSICS LAB ===")
print(f"Initial Query Cached:      {cached1}")
print(f"Second Query Cached:       {cached2} (Identity Map Hit)")
print(f"Same Instance in Memory:   {user1 is user2}")
print(f"User 2 Sees Mutation:      {user2['name']}")
user3, cached3 = identity_map.load("User", 43, "Bob")
print(f"PK 43 Cached Hit: {cached3} | Distinct From PK 42: {user3 is not user1} | Count: {len(identity_map.map)}")
print("Identity Map guarantees single-instance object coherence.")
checks: PK 43 Cached Hit: False | Distinct From PK 42: True | Count: 2

entries.partTitle: Long-Lived Session Memory Leak & Dirty State Forensics

spec.title: Global long-lived session vs request-scoped cleanup

steps.caption: Global sessions accumulate every row inside unbounded worker caches.
Uncommitted failed mutations from earlier callers leak on later commits.
Ephemeral session closing clears dirty state and frees RAM cleanly.
Call session.close() per request to wipe identity_map and dirty_queue.

checks: Leaked Cache Mode: identity_map=2 keys preserved
left.whatIf:
class SessionLifecycleSimulator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.identity_map = {}
        self.dirty_queue = []

    def process_request(self, user_id, new_email, should_commit=True):
        # Simulate loading into identity map
        entity = {"id": user_id, "email": new_email}
        self.identity_map[user_id] = entity
        self.dirty_queue.append(entity)
        if should_commit:
            self.dirty_queue.clear()  # Flushed

# Bad: Long-lived session accumulating state
global_session = SessionLifecycleSimulator()
# Request 1: Fails before commit
global_session.process_request("usr_101", "unvalidated@hack.com", should_commit=False)
# Request 2: Succeeds and commits
global_session.process_request("usr_202", "valid@work.com", should_commit=True)

print("=== SESSION CONTAMINATION FORENSICS ===")
print(f"Leaked Cache Mode: identity_map={len(global_session.identity_map)} keys preserved")
print(f"Total Tracked Entities:    {len(global_session.identity_map)} (RAM Leak Risk)")
print(f"Uncommitted Dirty Leftover: {len(global_session.dirty_queue)} items")
print("Long-lived sessions cause state contamination and memory bloat.")

spec.title: UnitOfWorkSession flush and SQL emission flow

steps.caption: New objects register in pending queues before database primary keys exist.
Session flush emits INSERT and targeted UPDATE statements atomically.
Second flush writes only mutated fields before clearing dirty state.
Add deleted list and emit SQL DELETE while removing from identity_map.

filled.title: UnitOfWorkSession flush and SQL emission flow

steps.caption: New objects register in pending queues before database primary keys exist.
Session flush emits INSERT and targeted UPDATE statements atomically.
Second flush writes only mutated fields before clearing dirty state.
Add deleted list and emit SQL DELETE while removing from identity_map.
steps.whatIf:
class UnitOfWorkSession:
    def __init__(self):
        self.identity_map = {}  # pk -> entity
        self.pending = []       # new objects
        self.dirty = set()
        self.deleted = []
        self.emitted_sql = []

    def mark_deleted(self, pk):
        self.deleted.append(pk)

    def add(self, entity):
        self.pending.append(entity)

    def mark_dirty(self, pk):
        self.dirty.add(pk)

    def flush(self):
        # 1. Emit INSERTs for pending
        for p in self.pending:
            self.emitted_sql.append(f"INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES ({p['id']}, '{p['name']}')")
            self.identity_map[p['id']] = p
        self.pending.clear()
        # 2. Emit UPDATEs for dirty
        for pk in self.dirty:
            obj = self.identity_map[pk]
            self.emitted_sql.append(f"UPDATE users SET name='{obj['name']}' WHERE id={pk}")
        self.dirty.clear()
        for pk in self.deleted:
            self.emitted_sql.append(f"DELETE FROM users WHERE id={pk}")
            self.identity_map.pop(pk, None)
        self.deleted.clear()

uow = UnitOfWorkSession()
uow.add({"id": 10, "name": "Charlie"})
uow.flush()

# Modify persistent object
uow.identity_map[10]["name"] = "Charlie Chaplin"
uow.mark_dirty(10)
uow.flush()

print("=== UNIT OF WORK FLUSH ENGINE ===")
print(f"Emitted SQL Statements: {len(uow.emitted_sql)}")
print(f"Statement 1:            {uow.emitted_sql[0]}")
print(f"Statement 2:            {uow.emitted_sql[1]}")
uow.mark_deleted(10)
uow.flush()
print(f"Statement 3:            {uow.emitted_sql[2]} | Remaining Map: {len(uow.identity_map)}")
print("Topological dirty state flushing executed successfully.")
checks: Statement 3:            DELETE FROM users WHERE id=10 | Remaining Map: 0

Network drops restore savepoint snapshots cleanly with zero partial debit.
Hardened transaction keeps debit, credit, and logs all-or-nothing.
Verify recipient balance stays preserved after rollback.

steps.whatIf:
class LedgerTransferEngine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.accounts = {"sender": 1000.0, "recipient": 200.0}

    def atomic_transfer(self, amount: float, simulate_crash=False):
        snapshot = dict(self.accounts)  # Savepoint
        try:
            # 1. Debit sender
            self.accounts["sender"] -= amount
            # 2. Simulate failure before recipient credit
            if simulate_crash:
                raise RuntimeError("Database connection dropped mid-transfer!")
            # 3. Credit recipient
            self.accounts["recipient"] += amount
            return True, "Committed"
        except Exception as e:
            # Unit of Work Rollback
            self.accounts = snapshot
            return False, f"Rolled back: {str(e)}"

engine = LedgerTransferEngine()
# Successful transfer
ok1, msg1 = engine.atomic_transfer(150.0, simulate_crash=False)
# Failing transfer with simulated network crash
ok2, msg2 = engine.atomic_transfer(300.0, simulate_crash=True)

print("=== FINANCIAL LEDGER ATOMICITY LAB ===")
print(f"Transfer 1 Success: {ok1} | Sender Bal: ${engine.accounts['sender']}")
print(f"Transfer 2 Success: {ok2} | Reason: {msg2}")
print(f"Sender Bal Preserved: ${engine.accounts['sender']} (No Orphaned Debit)")
print(f"Recipient Bal Preserved: ${engine.accounts['recipient']} (Rollback Shielded)")
print("ACID transactional atomicity verified under fault injection.")
